Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

adjust verb

also adapt, adjust to, fit (one thing to another), set (to the right level)

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.250: corōnam sibi ad caput (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 9.7: meum cōnsilium accommodābō ad tuum

accommodō, accommodāre, accommodāvī, accommodātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive; ad + accusative or dative

adjust, fit, adapt (one thing to another)

Fitting a thing to something else, a garland to the head or one’s plans to a friend’s; with sē, to adjust oneself to someone, comply (Cic. Or. 24).

Other words

  • temperō, temperāre, temperāvī, temperātum — adjust to the right degree, regulate (heat, a mixture, water)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Hor. C. 3.19.6: quis aquam temperet ignibus (Lewis & Short)

    Properly to mix in due proportion; so to bring heat, water or a voice to the right measure. With the dative or ab it means to refrain from something.

Examples

  • meum cōnsilium accommodābō ad tuum

    I’ll fit my plan to yoursCic. Fam. 9.7

  • Aquam temperā, nē nimis calida sit.

    Adjust the water so it isn’t too hot.composed

See also vary, improve.

SourcesLewis & Short: accommodo · Lewis & Short: tempero

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
